Abstract

the density functional theory and the statistical associating fluid theories were used to establish an equation of state for a binary liquid-liquid interface, the parameters of the segments were correlated by simultaneously fitting saturated vapor pressure and liquid density data, the interfacial region was divided into many extremely narrow layers in equilibrium, and the chemical potential of each component in every layer of interfacial region are equal to each, and a constant was obtained by optimizing the thickness of the interface.
the interfacial tension of 16 binary liquid-liquid systems is predicted based on the density functional theory and the statistical associating fluid thermodynamic theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interfacial properties of binary systems.
a density functional theory (DFT) for the prediction of interfacial tension of liquid-liquid binary systems.
the interfacial tension prediction for binary liquid- liquid systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density functional theory is a promising method for predicting the interfacial tension of liquid-liquid systems, especially for binary systems.
the present model can be used to describe and predict the interfacial tension for binary liquid- liquid systems with high precision.
the DFT and SAFT EOS can be used to predict the interfacial tensions for binary liquid- liquid systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the density functional theory and S.A.F.T. can be combined to predict the interfacial tension for binary liquid- liquid system.
the density functional theory and the statistical associating fluid are powerful methods to predict the interfacial tension.
the DFT-SAPT can be applied successfully to binary liquid-liquid systems and can be used for the prediction of interfacial tension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interfacial tension can be calculated by the density profile of the interface, which is a direct result of the equation of state.
the interfacial tensions can be predicted from the density data of pure component and binary liquid-liquid systems by density functional theory.
the interfacial tension can be predicted by density functional theory.
